newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh ex-president gets bail on murder charge.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh ex-president gets bail on murder charge.

text.p: Bangladesh's jailed former President Hossain Mohammad Ershad was granted bail by a special court on Tuesday on charges of killing an army general in 1981, the official BSS news agency said.
Judge Abdul Majid granted bail to Ershad, the principal defendant in the case involving the murder of Major General Abul Manzur, after a nearly three-hour hearing, the agency said.

Manzur was the Bangladesh Army's garrison commander in Chittagong, where then-President General Ziaur Rahman, husband of former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia, was killed on May 30, 1981, in an army mutiny.
Lieutenant-General Ershad was then the army chief, and he later deposed Zia's vice-president and successor Justice Abdus Sattar in a 1982 bloodless coup.
Manzur held the port city for two days before the revolt was crushed by loyal troops.
He was arrested while fleeing, but a group of soldiers took him from police and brought him back to the barracks where he was shot.
Several army officers were court-martialled and executed for Zia's killing soon after the mutiny but the mystery over Manzur's death remained.
Manzur's elder brother, barrister Abul Mansoor, filed a suit in February 1995 accusing Ershad of being the main culprit.
Ershad was overthrown in an opposition-led popular revolt in December 1990 and sentenced to 10 years in prison the following June for possession of unlicensed firearms.
He was later charged in 16 more cases of corruption and misuse of power, but as of Tuesday he had obtained bail in all but three cases, his laweyrs said.
Last year the High Court quashed his 10-year sentence in the arms case.
The court granted Ershad parole before last June's general election, which he contested as chief of the opposition Jatiya party, which won five parliament seats.
He is still enjoying the parole that allows him to attend parliament.
"We expect he will get bail in the rest of the cases soon," one of his lawyers said on Tuesday without giving details.
